requirement:
Sections use `section`, named from whitespace-normalized heading text. ATX and
setext headings are supported. Content before the first heading can form an
anonymous section. Section nesting follows heading levels; other outline items
appear beneath their nearest enclosing container. Selectors follow
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`.
rationale:
The reviewed tests cover each obligation in `requirements.sdk.sources.markdown.sections`. I did not request any implementation source.

- **Kind and naming from whitespace-normalized heading text**
  - `markdown_profile_nests_sections_by_heading` in `outline/tests.rs` checks that `# Head  *one*` becomes `section[Head%20*one*]`. It also checks that the section's structural hash is unchanged when the heading's whitespace and paragraph layout are reflowed.
  - `markdown_sections_include_setext_headings_and_anonymous_preamble` checks that `Heading   words` becomes `section[Heading%20words]`.
  - `multiline_setext_sections_keep_original_source_spans_and_skip_code` checks that a multi-line setext heading `Títle\ntwo` becomes `Títle%20two`.
- **ATX and setext headings**
  - ATX headings appear in several tests.
  - Setext level 1 (`===`) is covered in `markdown_sections_include_setext_headings_and_anonymous_preamble`.
  - Setext level 2 (`---`) is covered in `markdown_heading_levels_resolve_encoded_duplicates_and_anonymous_items`.
  - Multi-line setext is covered in `multiline_setext_sections_keep_original_source_spans_and_skip_code`.
  - `multiline_setext_sections_keep_original_source_spans_and_skip_code` also checks that `===` inside a fenced code block is not treated as a heading.
- **Anonymous preamble section**
  - `markdown_sections_include_setext_headings_and_anonymous_preamble` checks a `section@…` for `intro`.
  - `markdown_heading_levels_resolve_encoded_duplicates_and_anonymous_items` checks a `section@…` for `préface`, with the selected text asserted.
  - `markdown_profile_nests_sections_by_heading` checks that preamble content after front matter becomes an anonymous section with a paragraph child.
- **Nesting by heading level**
  - A skipped level (`# Main` then `### Deep`) nests under `Main`.
  - Sibling `## Same` sections nest under `Main`.
  - A new `# End` pops back to the top level.
  - A setext level-2 section nests under `End`, and a later `## Peer` becomes its sibling under `End`.
  - Section text ranges end before the next same-or-shallower heading. For example, `# Last` is excluded from the `Títle two` section, and `second` is excluded from the first `Same` section.
- **Other items beneath the nearest enclosing container**
  - `paragraphs_and_nested_directives_have_independent_source_ranges` asserts the full parent-index, kind and line-range tuples. Paragraphs and blocks sit under the section, and a nested paragraph sits under its block.
  - `setext_sections_inside_directives_lists_and_quotes_retain_container_spans` checks setext sections inside a directive, a block quote and a list. Only the directive case has `/block@` in its selector.
  - `markdown_heading_levels_resolve_encoded_duplicates_and_anonymous_items` checks that a block appears at `section[End]/section[Level%20two]/block@…`.
- **Selector grammar** (cited `requirements.references.outline_selectors`)
  - Special characters `/ [ ] # @ %` in headings are percent-encoded.
  - Duplicate siblings get `#1` and `#2`.
  - `outline.resolve` and `select` round-trip selectors, and anonymous segments are checked as `kind@` plus 12 characters.

I found no named boundary or failure case that goes untested. The "can form an anonymous section" wording is a MAY, and the tests exercise it anyway. All tests carry `{test}` references to the subject, so there is no marking gap.
